title.en: Lesson 1. Movement with a Purpose: -(으)러 가다 / 오다

blocks.md:
To explain **why you are going or coming somewhere**, attach **-(으)러**:
- Stem without batchim / ending in ㄹ → **-러 가다/오다** *(보다 → 보러 가요, 놀다 → 놀러 가요)*
- Stem with batchim → **-으러 가다/오다** *(먹다 → 먹으러 가요)*

**CRITICAL RESTRICTION**: The verb at the end of the sentence **MUST be a movement verb** like **가다** (to go), **오다** (to come), or **다니다** (to commute/attend)!

head: Purpose
Movement Verb
Full Sentence
rows: 친구 **만나러 왔어요** (Came to meet a friend)
친구 집에 **놀러 가요** (Going over to hang out)

items.tip: I’m heading out to eat lunch.
I came here to meet a friend.
I attend an academy to learn Korean.

blocks.q: Why is "책을 읽으러 도서관에 갔어요" correct, but "책을 읽으러 도서관에서 앉았어요" wrong?
options: -(으)러 can ONLY be followed by movement verbs like 가다/오다/다니다
-(으)러 can only be used with food
-(으)러 can only be used in the morning
blocks.why: -(으)러 expresses movement purpose, so the main verb must be a movement verb like 가다/오다/다니다.

blocks.meaning: I am going to the cafe to meet a friend.
blocks.why: Because the destination verb is 가요, 만나러 가요 is the direct, natural pattern.

blocks.q: Put in order: "I went to the restaurant to eat lunch."

blocks.hint: Verbs ending in ㄹ take -러 directly: 놀- + -러 = 놀러
blocks.why: 놀다 ends in ㄹ, so it attaches -러 directly without 으: 놀러 가요.

blocks.q: I am going to the restaurant to eat lunch.

blocks.md:
What if your main action is **NOT** a movement verb? *(“I bought a gift to give to my friend”)*

For general intentions with **ANY action verb**, use **-(으)려고**:
- *“친구에게 주**려고** 선물을 샀어요.”* (Bought a gift in order to give it — 샀어요 is not a movement verb!)

And when combined with **하다**, **-(으)려고 하다** means **“I plan to / I intend to...”**:
- *“새 컴퓨터를 사**려고 해요**.”* (I plan to buy a new computer.)

items.tip: I bought a present to give to my friend.
I came to Korea to learn Korean.
I am planning to buy a new computer.

blocks.q: Which sentence correctly says "I bought a present to give to my friend"?
blocks.why: Because 샀어요 is not a movement verb (like 가다/오다), you cannot use -러. You must use -(으)려고!

blocks.meaning: This weekend, I plan to rest at home.
blocks.why: 쉬려고 해요 expresses an intention or plan to rest.

blocks.q: Put in order: "I bought a gift to give to my friend."

blocks.wrong: 한국 친구를 사귀러 한국어를 열심히 공부해요.
answers: 한국 친구를 사귀려고 한국어를 열심히 공부해요.
한국 친구를 사귀려고 한국어를 열심히 공부해요
blocks.hint: 공부하다 is not a movement verb! Use -(으)려고: 사귀려고
blocks.why: 공부하다 is not a movement verb, so you cannot use -러. Use 사귀려고.

blocks.q: I plan to buy a new computer.

blocks.md:
When you make up your mind or agree with someone on a plan, use **-기로 하다** (*“decided to do”*).

Since decisions happen in the past, it is almost always said as **-기로 했어요**:

- *“내일부터 매일 운동하**기로 했어요**.”* (I decided to work out every day starting tomorrow.)
- *“주말에 친구를 만나**기로 했어요**.”* (I promised/decided to meet a friend on the weekend.)

Attach **-기로 하다** directly to the verb stem without any batchim changes!

items.tip: I decided to exercise starting tomorrow.
I decided to meet my friend this weekend.
I decided to study Korean diligently.

blocks.q: How do you say "We decided to meet at 2 PM tomorrow"? (내일 오후 2시에 만나다)
blocks.why: -기로 했어요 expresses an agreed decision or resolution: 만나기로 했어요.

blocks.meaning: For my health, I decided to exercise every day.
blocks.why: 운동하기로 했어요 represents a firm personal decision.

blocks.q: Put in order: "We decided to watch a movie on the weekend."

blocks.hint: Attach -기로 했어요: 일어나- + -기로 했어요 = 일어나기로 했어요
blocks.why: Attach -기로 directly to the stem: 일어나기로 했어요.

blocks.q: We decided to meet at 2 o'clock tomorrow.

title.ko: 4강. 세 가지 표현 가르기: -(으)러 vs -(으)려고 vs -기로 하다
title.en: Lesson 4. Comparing Purpose: -(으)러 vs -(으)려고 vs -기로 하다

blocks.md:
In the previous lessons, you learned three expressions expressing purpose and future plans. How do you choose between them?

1. **-(으)러 가다 / 오다** — **Only with movement verbs** (*to go/come in order to...*).
   - 도서관에 공부하**러 가요**. (O)
   - 공부하**러** 책을 샀어요. (X — 사다 is not movement!)

2. **-(으)려고** — **General intention with any action** (*in order to, intending to...*).
   - 공부하**려고** 책을 샀어요. (O)

3. **-기로 했어요** — **A firm decision or promise** (*decided to...*).
   - 주말에 친구를 만나**기로 했어요**.

head: Pattern
Meaning
Crucial Rule
rows: **Only** pairs with movement verbs (가다, 오다, 다니다)
Pairs with **any** action verb (책을 사다, 돈을 모으다)

items.tip: I am going to a café to meet a friend. (Movement)
I am saving money intending to go to Korea. (General action)
I decided to exercise early in the morning starting tomorrow. (Decision)

blocks.q: Why is 「책을 읽으러 도서관에서 책을 빌렸어요」 incorrect in natural Korean?
options: -(으)러 can only be followed by movement verbs like 가다 or 오다.
-(으)러 can only be used with food and eating.
-(으)러 cannot be attached to verbs ending in consonant.
-(으)러 is only used in formal written Korean.
blocks.why: -(으)러 is strictly used with movement verbs like 가다, 오다, and 다니다. For other actions, use -(으)려고: 「책을 읽으려고 빌렸어요」.

blocks.meaning: I bought a pretty hat intending to gift it to a friend.
blocks.why: The main verb is 샀어요 (bought), not a movement verb, so use -(으)려고 to express purpose.

blocks.q: 가다 (to go) — Complete the decision: 「내년 봄에 한국에 ___ . (decided to go)」
blocks.why: To state a firm decision or resolution, attach -기로 했어요 to the verb stem 가-.

blocks.q: Choose the natural sentence for going to a restaurant to eat lunch:
blocks.why: 먹으러 가요 correctly combines the purpose 먹다 with the movement verb 가다.

blocks.q: Put the words in order: "I am studying hard to pass the exam."
